# Part 3

Functions
- round()

```{r}

print(round(3.14159))

round(3.14159)

round(3.14159, digits = 2)


```

- seq() generates a sequence of number with arguments: from - to - by
- rep() repeats a value with argument : x (number) and times (number of times)

When writing a function call in RStudio, press the Tab key after the opening bracket (() to see a list of the arguments available for that function.

```{r}
seq(1,10,2)
print(seq(by = 2, from = 1, to = 10))

rep(5,7)
rep(x=5, times = 7)

```
```{r}
x <- 3.55
y <- "apple"
z <- TRUE

print(x)
print (y)
print(z)

class(x)
class(y)
class(z)

```

# Part 4

install.packages("") and then load by library()
```{r}
install.packages("fortunes")
library(fortunes)

fortune()
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
```

Vectors = multiple variables, everything needs to be the same type.

```{r}
my_first_vector <- c(1, 5, 9)
print(my_first_vector)
```

```{r}
cell_ID <- c(cell_ID_1,cell_ID_2)
treated <- c( treated_1, treated_2)
num_before <- c(num_before_1, num_before_2)
num_after <- c(num_after_1, num_after_2)

print(cell_ID)
print(treated)
print(num_before)
print(num_after)
```

Once our values are in a vector, we can access them using an index, which refers to the position of the value within the vector. Indices are indicated within square brackets - []

```{r}
all_my_pets <- c("dog", "horse", "guinea pig", "chicken", "cat")
pet_4 <- all_my_pets[4]
print(pet_4)
```

Vectorisation : apply same function to many variable in a vector at once

```{r}
x <- c(2, -4, 6, -2)
x * 2
x > 5
sum(x)
abs(x)
```

Data frame

```{r}

data_frame <- tibble(
   fruit = c("apple", "pear", "banana"),
  length = c(22, 30, 55),
  weight = c(150, 165, 170)
)

print(data_frame)

gt(data_frame)
```

```{r}

prac1_table <- tibble(
  
    cell_ID = c(cell_ID_1, cell_ID_2),
    treated = c(treated_1, treated_2),
    num_before = c(num_before_1, num_before_2),
    num_after = c(num_after_1, num_after_2)
)

gt(prac1_table)
```
